result.label: Own-price elasticity, 330ml can
result.rationale: Smallest, most impulse-driven format; set near the elastic end of the brief's -0.8 to -2.5 CPG range.
result.reference: Context only, not a fitted value. A 2024 meta-analysis of U.S. food demand elasticities (Jeon, Hoang, Thompson and Abler) finds household scanner data tends to give more elastic own-price estimates (https://pure.psu.edu/en/publications/a-meta-analysis-of-us-food-demand-elasticities-to-detect-the-impa/). It does not cover soft drinks specifically, so the values here are illustrative. A Marketing Science Institute working paper (Bray, Sanders and Stamatopoulos) finds observational scanner price variation does not reproduce experimental elasticities (https://www.msi.org/working-paper/observational-price-variation-in-scanner-data-cannot-reproduce-experimental-price-elasticities/), so the value carries a range that drives the sensitivity bands.

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: At the current Aurora 330 ml can price, the brand earns a weekly gross profit of ₹227,764 on the baseline scenario.

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: With the modest list price increase on the Aurora 330 ml can, the brand’s modeled weekly gross profit falls slightly to ₹226,442, as the can price gain is more than offset by the can’s volume loss despite some shoppers shifting into other Aurora packs.

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: Under the aggressive price increase on the Aurora 330 ml can, the modeled weekly gross profit falls further to ₹224,296, because the larger price rise causes a bigger volume drop on the can that the additional price and cost benefits do not fully offset.

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: With the mid-level price increase plus light promotion on the Aurora 330 ml can, the modeled weekly gross profit rises to ₹229,255, the highest of the tested options.

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: In the modest list price increase scenario, the Aurora 330 ml can’s weekly volume decreases versus baseline while staying within about a 5% loss.

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: In the aggressive price increase scenario, the Aurora 330 ml can’s weekly volume drops more sharply than in the modest increase scenario, pushing the volume loss further toward the 5% guardrail.

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: In the price rise with light promotion scenario, the Aurora 330 ml can’s weekly volume sits between the modest and aggressive increase scenarios, indicating that limited promotion support helps protect volume compared with an unsupported mid-level increase.

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: Relative to baseline, the modest list price increase changes the focal brand’s gross profit mainly through a positive price effect that is more than offset by a negative volume effect, with minor positive contributions from promotion, cross-pack shifts and cost of goods.

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: Relative to baseline, the aggressive price increase has a larger positive price effect on gross profit but an even larger negative volume effect, resulting in a net loss in gross profit versus the current price.

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: Relative to baseline, the price rise with light promotion includes a positive contribution from promotion and a positive price effect that, together with cross-pack shifts and small cost benefits, more than offset the negative volume effect to deliver a net gain in gross profit.

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: The downside input-cost stress scenario reduces the brand’s weekly gross profit versus baseline purely through higher cost of goods, with price, volume and promotion held constant.

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: The synthetic Gabor–Granger research proposed a 330 ml can candidate price of ₹36.00 as the revenue-index maximum in consumer responses.

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: The same synthetic research also identified ₹40.00 as the highest accepted 330 ml can price in consumer responses, which corresponds in the modeling to the current price scenario.

claims.label: Observed
claims.text: The Gabor–Granger revenue-index maximum price scenario, implying a lower list price for the Aurora 330 ml can, was refused by the modeling engine because the requested price cut lay outside the supported historical range and could not be simulated.

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: Among all supported options for the Aurora 330 ml can, the price rise with light promotion delivers the highest modeled weekly gross profit for the brand while keeping the can’s volume loss close to, but not materially beyond, the 5% tolerance band considered in this analysis.

claims.label: Recommended
claims.text: Given the modeled outcomes and the volume-loss guardrail, adopting the mid-level price increase with light promotion on the Aurora 330 ml can is preferable to both holding price flat and pushing through a more aggressive unsupported list price rise.

recommendations: Implement a mid-level price increase on the Aurora 330 ml can with light promotion support, as this delivers the highest weekly gross profit for the brand among the tested options while keeping can volume loss near your 5% tolerance.

Do not proceed with the more aggressive price increase on the Aurora 330 ml can, because it reduces weekly gross profit versus both baseline and the lighter price move for only a modest additional price benefit.

Use the current price as your control and track actual can and total-brand volumes closely if you move to the price rise with light support, to confirm that real-world volume loss stays within your 5% guardrail.
refusals: Aurora-can_330ml: price_index 0.9 outside observed 1st-99th percentile [0.9424, 1.1082]; this means the modeled system cannot support a cut to the Gabor-Granger revenue-index maximum price for the 330 ml can.
answer.summary:
Keep the current Aurora 330 ml can price and, if you want some upside, use the light-promotion price rise, because it gives the highest weekly gross profit for the brand while keeping the modeled volume loss on the can close to your 5% guardrail and avoiding heavier profit dilution elsewhere in the range tested.
- Baseline – current price: weekly gross profit ₹227,764; reference point with current volume and no promotion or cost shocks.
- Modest list price increase: weekly gross profit ₹226,442; slightly lower profit than baseline as the price gain on the can is more than offset by volume loss on the can and only modest benefits from shoppers moving into other Aurora packs.
- Aggressive price increase: weekly gross profit ₹224,296; lowest profit among supported price-up moves because the larger price gain cannot compensate for the bigger drop in can volume even after some trade and cost benefits.
- Price rise with light support: weekly gross profit ₹229,255; best option because a mid-level list price increase plus limited promotion lifts revenue and protects volume better, with promotion and small cross-pack gains more than covering the volume loss.
